OFFICE OF THE SUPERVISOR
TOWN OF SOUTHOLD

Members of the Southold Town Board:
| respectfully submit the Supervisor’s Tentative Budget for the fiscal year 2027.
Overall, the Town’s fiscal position is strong, thanks to careful management of departmental
growth and overall spending.
The proposed Tentative Budget for 2027 offers a realistic approach to delivering services
and managing operations that reflect our quality of life. New York State has set a cap on
local government spending, which does not reflect the reality of many expenses that are
outside our control. The NYS Tax Cap also doesn’t reflect the growing number of unfunded
State mandates that negatively affect the Town’s budget. Nevertheless, it serves as a
benchmark we strive to remain under, as a measure of sound budgeting and responsible
management.
My goal is always to spend as little taxpayer money as possible while still delivering the
necessary services. This budget reflects that philosophy and does not pierce the cap.
| remain committed to keeping our fleet up to date. Our small town operates many vehicles
that must be replaced regularly. Our investment in a new highway barn will help extend the
life of both our newest trucks and equipment, as well as our older vehicles. This budget
reflects my commitment to replacing vehicles and improving the management of the
existing fleet.
The budget reflects our commitment to public safety by maintaining proper police staffing
levels and providing officers with the necessary equipment and training. Previous budgets
relied on federal ARPA funds to support recurring expenses, such as police vehicles. These
critical vehicles are now included in this budget.
| remain dedicated to maintaining our beaches and public spaces, which are cherished
parts of our community. They require significant funding and management. | want to thank
the Recreation Department, Police Department, Engineering Department, Department of

Public Works, Highway Department, and Government Liaison for their efforts. Our beaches
are clean and well-managed, thank you.
The 2027 Tentative Budget cannot rely on ARPA funds. Forecasted sales tax revenue has
not increased, and mortgage tax revenue has significantly decreased.
Revenues increased in 2026, but the cost of operations outpaced all expectations. Labor
contract costs, increase in fuel for fleet and heating, overall inflated cost for all materials,
goods and services are all having an impact on this years' budget.
Settlements of inherited lawsuits from the past administration has drained the contingency
fund for 2026.
This Town must continually evaluate how money is spent, as tomorrow’s needs will differ
from yesterday’s challenges.
Staffing changes include a full-time Director of Code Enforcement, reflecting the Town’s
commitment to community housing. Meaningful code changes are underway to support
housing initiatives, but the control and regulation of short-term rentals require real
oversight. These changes will benefit the safety of the tenants, reduce the burden on first
responders, and address the quality of life of our residents.
| am grateful to all Departments Heads for their careful management and cooperation
throughout the budget process. All 217 full-time employees and 49 part-time employees
are partners in this budget, and | appreciate their hard work.
| also thank the Town Board. As demand for services increases, they remain strong partners
in making difficult decisions to control spending and keep us under the tax cap this year.
There are always unforeseen challenges in running a Town, as in life. No one planned for
the impacts of a major computer hack, but it demonstrated the competence of our
employees, who continued serving the public, while working closely with our partners of
other levels of government.
We can plan on Nor’easters, hurricanes, aging vehicles that require replacement, building
maintenance and public safety needs. All of these challenges are addressed in this budget.
As a resident, | want services delivered for the least amount of money. If we expect families
to live here in the future—working in this Town and building their lives here—we must
control the size of government and its associated costs.

Comptroller Sharon Glassman, Secretarial Assistant to the Town Board Michelle
Tomaszewski, Secretarial Assistant to the Supervisor Lauren Standish, and Deputy
Supervisor John Stype for their hard work and valuable contributions in helping deliver this
budget to the residents of Southold Town.
Each year’s budget presents new challenges, and | look forward to working on the 2028
budget.
Respectfully submitted,
